results.title: Evaluating a propositional formula at a letter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A letter is a set $s$ of atoms (the atoms true at it). A propositional formula is evaluated at $s$ by recursion: an atom $a$ is true iff $a \in s$, truth $\top$ is true, $\neg\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is not, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is true iff both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are true.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The translation of propositional formulas into LTL formulas is defined by recursion: an atom $a$ goes to the LTL atom $a$, truth goes to the LTL truth constant $\top$, $\neg\varphi$ goes to the LTL negation of the translation of $\varphi$, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$ goes to the LTL conjunction of the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$.

results.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the first letter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it belongs to that letter, $w$ satisfies the LTL translation of $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ evaluates to true on the first letter $w_0$.

results.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the current letter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula, let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms, and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. results.title: Büchi automaton for a propositional formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, this Büchi automaton over letters that are sets of atoms has a start state $u$ and two verdict states $t$ and $f$, of which only $t$ is accepting. From $u$, on a letter $s$ it moves to $t$ if $\varphi$ evaluates to true at $s$ and to $f$ otherwise; from $t$ and from $f$ it stays in the same state on every letter. So it records the verdict of $\varphi$ on the first letter.

results.title: No infinite group has equicardinal maximal direct factors

results.title: Encodings of a class of ordered graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a class $K$ of ordered graphs, this is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a natural number and a list of booleans, to some $G \in K$ whose edge table has length exactly $n^2$, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $G$.

results.title: Definability in FO + LFP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class $K$ of ordered graphs is definable in first-order logic with least fixed points when there are a formula $\varphi$ and a boolean $b$ such that every ordered graph $G$ with $n$ vertices whose edge table has length $n^2$ lies in $K$ exactly when either $n > 0$ and $G$ satisfies $\varphi$, or $n = 0$ and $b$ is true.

results.title: Page served by a cache event
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The page served by a cache event is the page it requests, whether the event is a hit or a miss.

results.title: Miss indicator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The miss indicator of a cache event is true if the event is a miss and false if it is a hit.

results.title: Number of misses in a trace
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of misses of a finite list of cache events is the number of events in the list that are misses.

results.title: Legal cache transitions preserve valid caches
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and let $C \to C'$ be a legal cache transition for capacity $k$, labelled by any cache event. If $C$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$, then $C'$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$.

results.title: Legal cache traces preserve valid caches
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and suppose a finite sequence of cache events leads from the cache $C$ to the cache $C'$ by legal cache transitions for capacity $k$. If $C$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$, then $C'$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$.

results.title: A legal step caches the served page
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k > 0$ be a capacity. If a legal transition for capacity $k$ takes a cache $C$ to a cache $C'$ by a cache event, then the page served by that event lies in $C'$.

results.title: A legal trace without misses serves only cached pages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity. If a legal trace of cache events for capacity $k$ starts from a cache $C$ and contains no miss, then every page served by an event of the trace lies in $C$.

results.title: A legal trace misses at least once
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and $C$ a cache listing at most $k$ pages, and consider a legal trace of cache events for capacity $k$ that starts from $C$. Let $p$ be a page in $C$. If at least $k + 1$ distinct pages are each equal to $p$ or served by some event of the trace, then the trace contains at least one miss.

results.title: Furthest-in-future serves exactly the requests
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $R$ a list of requested blocks and $C$ a duplicate-free list of blocks of length at most $k$. Then the events emitted by the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ on $R$ from the initial cache $C$ serve, in order, exactly the blocks of $R$.
